papers_read.title_as_printed: Early diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease using multimodal feature-based deep learning models in a Chinese elderly population (Wang et al., Asian Journal of Psychiatry 2025)
A method for diagnosis support of mild cognitive impairment through EEG rhythms source location during working memory tasks (San-Martin et al., Biomed Signal Process Control 66 (2021) 102499)

what_each_reports.P-133: The 72.67 +/-1.89% the record cites is THREE-CLASS HC/MCI/AD accuracy (GCN, Neutral stimulus; ERP differential entropy + TCM questionnaire features; 30/30/30; cross-subject 10-fold). The binary result nearest to T1 is HC vs MCI+AD pooled: 89.22 +/-1.90% in Table 2 (the abstract says 90.17 +/-5.58%, an inconsistency within the paper). No HC-vs-MCI-only task is reported.
what_each_reports.P-114: The record's claim (93% accuracy, T1) and the P-114 summary block describe a Kinect V2 gait + ANFIS study (block header file 1-s2.0-S1746809421003195-main.pdf). That PDF is not in downloads/. The PDF supplied as P-114 (map entry, DOI 10.1016/j.bspc.2021.102499) is a different paper: EEG LORETA source CSD during an N-back task, 19 MCI vs 22 HE, SVM 96% epoch-level accuracy (WME alone 0.93).

quantity_a: As cited: three-class HC/MCI/AD accuracy from ERP+TCM features. Nearest binary: HC vs pooled MCI+AD
quantity_b: As recorded: MCI vs healthy elderly accuracy from Kinect gait features (source document unavailable). Supplied PDF: epoch-level MCI vs HE accuracy from task-EEG source features
incompatible_if_same: Not assessable as a contradiction. P-133's cited value is three-class, and its binary value pools MCI with AD against controls, so neither is an MCI-vs-control accuracy. Whichever P-114 paper is meant, the comparison class differs.

gates.task: mismatch: the cited P-133 value is ternary. Its binary task is HC vs MCI+AD, not MCI vs HC.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: Zhejiang clinic/community cohort vs a separate clinical cohort (Kinect study per block; Montreal JGH/Concordia in the supplied PDF)
gates.modality_family: mismatch: ERP + TCM questionnaires vs gait kinematics (per block). The supplied PDF is task EEG, which is closer in modality but still a different quantity.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: three-class accuracy (or HC vs pooled impaired) vs binary MCI-vs-control accuracy
performance_validity: flag does not apply to P-133. The supplied P-114 PDF reports 96% epoch-level accuracy (below 0.97, but classified per epoch, not per patient). The Kinect paper cannot be checked.
grounds: The record's claim_a misreads P-133: 72.67% is three-class HC/MCI/AD accuracy, not a T1 (MCI vs controls) result.
P-133's binary result pools MCI with AD against controls, so no P-133 figure estimates MCI-vs-control accuracy. The pair therefore has no shared quantity whatever P-114's value is.
The PDF supplied for P-114 is the wrong paper: the record and summary block describe a Kinect gait/ANFIS study not held in downloads/. This does not affect the verdict, which rests on P-133's side.

resolution_note 'Task mismatch from summaries: T1_mci_vs_hc vs T2_conversion' fits neither paper: neither P-133 nor either P-114 candidate is a conversion study.

what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing on P-133's side, since no MCI-vs-control accuracy exists in it. Recovering the Kinect PDF would settle the P-114 value but could not create a shared quantity.
